leads.headline: Attacks on Shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
leads.body: Fresh attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz raised fears for global energy supplies, as Iran vowed to use all available means against a US blockade. A Houthi strike on Riyadh and interceptions over Saudi Arabia put a second sea lane, the Red Sea, under threat as well.

leads.headline: Ukraine Sinks Russian Warship in a Libyan Port
leads.body: Ukrainian drones sank a Russian warship in Benghazi and hit cargo ships from the Mediterranean to the Baltic, in Kyiv's longest-range campaign of the war. Two Libyan naval officers were killed, raising fears of a wider Mediterranean escalation.

leads.headline: Zelensky: Ukraine Needs €115 Billion for 2027
leads.body: Kyiv says it needs €115 billion in foreign aid to fund the state and the war through 2027. The appeal landed as the US defence secretary paused Patriot missile supplies and Washington shelved proposals to end the war through business deals with Russia.

leads.headline: Pakistan's First Astronaut Reaches China's Space Station
leads.body: China launched a crewed spaceship carrying Pakistan's first astronaut to its orbiting space station, a milestone watched live across Pakistan. The flight deepens the two countries' space partnership and gives Islamabad its first human presence in orbit.

leads.headline: Australia Signs Landmark Treaty with Solomon Islands
leads.body: Australia and Solomon Islands signed a major treaty that strengthens Canberra's security position in the Pacific. The pact reshapes regional alignments as Pacific capitals weigh competing partnerships and promises.

leads.headline: US Jury Convicts Huawei of Stealing Trade Secrets
leads.body: A New York jury found Huawei guilty of conspiring to steal trade secrets, though it acquitted the Chinese firm of racketeering. Beijing accused Washington of obstructing Chinese companies, in the latest legal clash of the tech cold war.

leads.headline: Anthropic Shares Fall Below Their IPO Price
leads.body: Anthropic's stock dropped below its market launch price for the first time, wiping out its $1 trillion valuation as AI fears returned to Wall Street. Asian markets fell first, and US futures followed them lower.

leads.headline: Colombia Frees All Hostages in Supermarket Siege
leads.body: Colombian security forces stormed a Cartagena supermarket and freed every hostage, ending a siege that had gripped the country. President Petro said one assailant was killed and all the captives came out alive.

leads.headline: Court Gives Senegal Its Africa Cup Title Back
leads.body: Sport's highest court ruled for Senegal on appeal, restoring its 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title. Morocco, stripped of the crown by the ruling, vowed to challenge it.

leads.headline: UK Energy Bills to Jump 26% in January
leads.body: Regulator Ofgem is raising the energy price cap as gas prices surge, lifting a typical annual bill from £1,723 to £2,166. The rise lands in January, the coldest and darkest month of the British winter.

briefs.headline: EURO INFLATION
briefs.body: Inflation across the euro area rose to 4.0%, Eurostat reported, as growth, jobs and production data painted a mixed picture.

briefs.headline: AUSTRALIA PRICES
briefs.body: Australian inflation climbed to 4.9% on fuel costs, though the central bank is still expected to hold interest rates.

briefs.headline: EU TECH FUND
briefs.body: The European Union is planning a €50 billion technology fund designed to challenge the dominance of the US and China.

briefs.headline: GTA VI
briefs.body: GTA VI's $3.79 billion debut had Zuckerberg joking and Musk laughing, but Take-Two investors still want more.

briefs.headline: EASYJET
briefs.body: EasyJet's profit fell 89% after a £244 million fuel-cost hit; the airline is speeding up retirement of its oldest aircraft.

briefs.headline: AMAZON BUYS DECART
briefs.body: Amazon bought AI startup Decart, a bet that better software can help its own chips compete with Nvidia's.

briefs.headline: AI-AGENT HACK
briefs.body: Amazon says attackers used AI agents, with little human input, to break into a university server through a previously unknown flaw.

briefs.headline: CIA BREACH
briefs.body: Hackers breached unclassified CIA and ODNI intelligence-analysis systems, the New York Times reported.

briefs.headline: GAZA
briefs.body: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed seven people, including a senior security official.

briefs.headline: RIYADH
briefs.body: A Houthi attack injured 11 people in Riyadh, two of them Indian; the Saudi-led coalition intercepted further attacks after striking Hodeidah.

briefs.headline: KOREA
briefs.body: South Korea said Russian jets entered its air defence identification zone.

briefs.headline: NORTH KOREA
briefs.body: North Korea declared a Swiss diplomat persona non grata and ordered him to leave the country.

briefs.headline: XI PURGE
briefs.body: Xi Jinping's anti-corruption purge took down Chen Jining, Shanghai's party chief and a rising political star.

briefs.headline: BANGLADESH
briefs.body: Bangladesh garment workers won a 36% pay rise after weeks of protests.

briefs.headline: INDONESIA MINE
briefs.body: Rescuers searched for dozens of miners trapped in a flooded gold mine in Indonesia.

briefs.headline: HIV WARNING
briefs.body: The UN warned that funding cuts threaten decades of progress in the fight against HIV and AIDS.

briefs.headline: ÁBREGO GARCÍA
briefs.body: Kilmar Ábrego García left the US for Spain, ending a 20-month legal fight that made him a symbol of Trump-era deportations.

briefs.headline: GIVING
briefs.body: After $26 billion in gifts, MacKenzie Scott gave Atlanta students $8 million more — and is still worth $27 billion.
